issues.detail: Example 1 is a prose description of UI steps and expected outcomes, and Example 2 gives no CI job snippet or status-polling code, so neither shows concrete runnable output.

scenarios.name: deploy-pentagi-with-secure-env
scenarios.rationale: Both set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, fetch .env and docker-compose.yml, run docker compose up -d, set PENTAGI_LISTEN_IP/PUBLIC_URL/CORS_ORIGINS, and firewall 8443; A also covers the Neo4j password and tells the user to change the default login, while B omits Neo4j and adds extras like embeddings, but its hedging about recall is slightly weaker.

scenarios.name: trigger-flow-from-ci-via-api
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric point: the token is created under Settings → API Tokens and stored as a secret, the GraphQL createFlow call carries a Bearer header and a scope-limited prompt, it polls GET /api/v1/flows until the flow is finished, and it notes that -k is only for the default self-signed certificate. B polls via a GraphQL flow query instead of GET /api/v1/flows, never mentions -k, and hedges that its API details come from memory, though its scope-limited createFlow call and secret handling are fine.

scenarios.name: run-scoped-flow-and-handle-report
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric item (Automation flow, prompt with target/scope limits/confirmed findings with reproduction steps, Report menu download as Markdown or PDF with no JSON, LLM-generated findings needing manual verification, supervised run) with PentAGI-specific detail, while B stays generic, never mentions the Automation flow or the Report menu or export formats, and opens with a partial refusal, though it does cover supervision and hand-verification.
